settings.title: Network
settings.desc: Network mode, proxy configuration, and real IP protection. The popup's Network page switches modes quickly and can set the current site to direct or proxy.
settings.reloadOnSwitch: Refresh the page after switching proxies
settings.reloadOnSwitchHint: After switching network mode in the popup, automatically refresh the current page
settings.bypassTitle: Bypass list (domains that skip this proxy)
settings.bypassHint: One domain or Chrome proxy bypass rule per line. Proxy, Auto, and every custom proxy mode each save their own list.
settings.unsaved: Unsaved changes to the proxy server or bypass list. Save to apply them
settings.saveHint: Proxy server and bypass list changes need saving; the rule list, proxy domains, and the WebRTC settings below take effect immediately
settings.noConfigDesc: Direct and System proxy need no configuration. Switch to Auto, Global proxy, or a custom mode to configure the proxy server, rule list, and bypass list here.
settings.noConfig: Nothing to configure for this mode

proxyControl.notControllable: The browser doesn't allow extensions to control the proxy
proxyControl.byOther: The proxy is controlled by another extension

deleteMode.title: Delete custom proxy
deleteMode.name: "{name}"
deleteMode.desc: After deleting, it falls back to the built-in proxy configuration. Auto, Global proxy, and other custom modes are not affected.

controller.invalidProxy: Enter a valid proxy host and port
controller.invalidCustomProxy: Invalid proxy host or port in a custom mode
controller.nameRequired: Enter a name for the custom mode
controller.savedApplied: Saved and applied to the current mode
controller.savedSynced: Saved and synced to the current proxy
controller.hostBypassRemoved: This site no longer goes direct

configDesc.global: Global proxy · All traffic through the proxy

ruleList.title: Rule list
ruleList.hint: When enabled, sites matching a rule go through the proxy; the list updates automatically every 6 hours. With no rule list enabled and no custom proxy domains, Auto connects everything directly.
ruleList.downloadFailed: Failed to download the rule list
ruleList.updated: Updated {proxy} proxy rules and {direct} direct exceptions

scenario.title: Custom proxy domains
scenario.desc: Sites that need the proxy but aren't covered by the rule list
scenario.hint: One domain per line, subdomains included automatically. Takes priority over the rule list and saves on blur.
scenario.hostProxied: {host} and its subdomains will go through the proxy

defaultAction.title: When no rule matches
defaultAction.proxyHint: Everything goes through the proxy except the bypass list, LAN, and .cn domains. Best when your proxy app handles its own routing
defaultAction.directHint: Only sites matching a rule go through the proxy; everything else connects directly
defaultAction.proxyStatus: Requests matching no rule will go through the proxy
defaultAction.directStatus: Requests matching no rule will connect directly

cors.title: Disable CORS restrictions (turn off the browser's cross-origin blocking)
cors.desc: Adds cross-origin response headers to the page's XHR/fetch responses
cors.note: For local development and debugging only. Can't fix servers that reject OPTIONS, credentialed requests, CSP, or mixed-content restrictions. Refresh the page after toggling.
cors.enabled: CORS headers are being added to the page's XHR/fetch responses
cors.failed: Failed to enable. Check the extension's permissions or reload the extension

webrtc.title: Real IP protection
webrtc.intro: With a proxy on, sites can still use the browser's WebRTC (the tech behind in-page audio/video calls) to bypass the proxy and quietly get your real IP — and from it guess your city and carrier. With protection on, sites only see the proxy's IP.
webrtc.scope: Applies only to web pages in this browser, not to other apps on your computer. Pages asking for location permission (precise location) prompt separately through the browser and aren't controlled here. Settings on this page save immediately — no need to click "Save and apply" above.
webrtc.permissionRequired: The "Change privacy settings" permission is required to enable protection

default.label: Off (browser default)
default.hint: Pages can quietly get your real IP and LAN addresses, even with a proxy on

hideVpn.label: Hide VPN / virtual adapters
hideVpn.hint: Stops exposing extra adapters like VPNs and virtual machines; your real IP and LAN addresses remain visible

hideLan.label: Hide LAN addresses
hideLan.hint: Pages can't see your home or office network addresses. Your real IP is still visible, and in-page video calls keep working

hideRealIp.label: Hide real IP (recommended)
hideRealIp.hint: With a proxy on, pages only see the proxy's IP and can't infer your real location or carrier. A few in-page video calls may slow down or fail to connect

control.byOther: Controlled by another extension (e.g. WebRTC Control). DevGo's settings won't take effect — disable that extension first
control.byOtherShort: Controlled by another extension; protection not active
control.locked: Locked by browser policy; the extension can't change it
control.lockedShort: Locked by browser policy; protection not active

impact.unaffectedDownload: Regular browsing, watching videos, downloads, and client apps on your computer are unaffected.
impact.undoPolicy: If in-page calls misbehave, set the level back to "Off" to restore.
impact.undoToggle: Turn this toggle off and refresh the page to restore.

hideVpn.title: Turn on "Hide VPN / virtual adapters"
hideVpn.action: Changes the browser's WebRTC settings so pages can only use the default network adapter; addresses of extra adapters like VPNs and VMs are no longer exposed to pages. Applies to all pages.
hideVpn.affect1: In-page calls that only connect through a VPN or virtual adapter may fail to connect

hideLan.title: Turn on "Hide LAN addresses"
hideLan.action: Changes the browser's WebRTC settings so pages get only your public address, not your home or office LAN address. Applies to all pages.
hideLan.affect1: Calls and P2P file transfer within the same Wi-Fi / LAN can't connect directly and reroute through the internet, possibly a bit slower
hideLan.affect2: In-page meeting systems that only work on an intranet may fail to connect

hideRealIp.title: Turn on "Hide real IP"
hideRealIp.action: Changes the browser's WebRTC settings (disallowing UDP connections that bypass the proxy), so pages' audio/video connections must go through the proxy and sites can't get your real IP. Applies to all pages.
hideRealIp.affect1: In-browser video meetings and voice calls (Tencent Meeting / Feishu / Google Meet web, etc.) may slow down, stutter, or fail — more so if the proxy doesn't support UDP
hideRealIp.affect2: In-page P2P file transfer, live-stream chat, and real-time connections in some web games
hideRealIp.affect3: With no proxy on, some in-page calls may also fail to connect
hideRealIp.unaffected: Regular browsing, watching videos, downloads, and client apps on your computer (like meeting clients) are unaffected.
hideRealIp.undo: If a web meeting won't connect, try setting the level back to "Off" first. The popup's Network page shows whether protection is on.

blockApis.title: Disable in-page audio/video calls
blockApis.action: Removes WebRTC interfaces (RTCPeerConnection etc.) before each page loads, so sites can't establish audio/video connections at all — and can't get any of your IPs. Applies to all pages; takes effect after a refresh.
blockApis.affect1: All in-browser video meetings, voice calls, and screen sharing stop working; sites may say "browser not supported"
blockApis.affect2: In-page P2P file transfer, live-stream chat, and voice/video calls in online support chats

hideDevices.title: Hide camera and microphone
hideDevices.action: Blocks the media-device interfaces before each page loads, so sites can't see which cameras and microphones you have or use them. Applies to all pages; takes effect after a refresh.
hideDevices.affect1: Cameras and microphones won't open in web meetings
hideDevices.affect2: In-page recording, filming, photo upload, voice input, and identity verification
hideDevices.unaffected: Regular browsing, watching videos, and client apps on your computer are unaffected.

level.title: Protection level
level.label: Level
level.hint: Applies to all pages. The first time you enable it, the browser asks for the "Change privacy settings" permission
level.enabledTip: On: if web meetings or voice calls won't connect, try setting the level back to "Off" first.
level.notGranted: Not granted yet, so protection isn't active. Pick the level again to grant it
level.unsupported: This browser doesn't support this setting

strict.title: Stricter blocking
strict.desc: Turns the relevant features off in pages outright — no site can get around it, but those features stop working. Refresh pages after changing.
strict.blockApisHint: Sites can't get any of your IP; in-browser meetings, voice calls, and P2P file transfer stop working
strict.hideDevicesHint: Sites can't see which devices you have (often used to identify and track your computer), so camera and microphone won't work

leakTest.title: Run a check
leakTest.desc: Try it once on a page you have open to see which addresses sites can actually get. With a proxy on, a real IP in the list means protection isn't working. Re-run after changing settings to compare.
leakTest.idle: Click "Start check". Results are what a site would see
leakTest.blocked: In-page audio/video calls are disabled; sites can't get any address

candidate.mdns: Local address (anonymized by the browser; safe)
candidate.public: Public IP (with a proxy on, this should be the proxy's IP)

status.notGranted: Not granted yet; protection isn't active
status.offWithProxy: Off: with a proxy on, sites may still see your real IP
status.off: Off: stop sites from bypassing your proxy to see your real IP
status.tooltip: Sites can use WebRTC to bypass the proxy and get your real IP. Click to enable protection in settings

background.proxyApiUnavailable: This browser doesn't support the chrome.proxy API, or the extension wasn't granted the proxy permission
background.ruleListHttpOnly: The rule list URL only supports http/https
background.ruleListInvalidUrl: Enter a valid rule list URL
background.leakTestNoTab: Open any web page (http/https) first, then come back to run the check
background.leakTestFailed: Couldn't run the check on this page: {message}
